Package model.description.abstraction

Class Placeholder

java.lang.Object
model.description.abstraction.Placeholder
public class Placeholder extends Object
A class used to join a described primitive with it's decoration elements: a handle, an offset point and it's bounds. It also contain functionality that makes it easy moving and resizing it's frame.

It was thoroughly considered wether this class was really necessary or if the described formal could manage this on its own. And the final conclusion was that place holder are necessary things.

    • Placeholder

      public Placeholder(Described primitive)
      Instantiates a new placeholder for a described formal's cursor and fills it.
      Parameters:
      primitive - A primitive that this placeholder will be fitted for and contain. The primitive is also inserted and there is no need to call insert afterwards. Yet, it is only described primitives that is considered but perhaps composites could useful as well.

  • Method Details

    • frame

      public DCursor frame()
      The rich cursor bounds of the bounding placeholder frame. Rich in the sense that it contains more varables and functionality than a simple rectangle.
      Returns:
      The rich rectangular bounds object.

    • described

      public Described described()
      The described formal, presumably a primitive, that is currently held by this placeholder.
      Returns:
      The described primitive or null if it is filled with null.

    • handle

      public Placeholder.Handle handle()
      The handle of the frame and eventually it's formal. The handle coincides with both's respective reference points, the write point where it all is written at. See FontMetrics.
      Returns:
      The handle the user clicks when moving the placeholder around. The handles makes up the mouse interactive area.

    • getLocalReference

      public Point2D.Double getLocalReference()
      The local write point offset, an offset from device coordinates origo. The write point is called reference point in java's and I guess in common typographical nomenclature and is at the start of the glyph's base line.
      Returns:
      The reference point, the write point of the placeholder and perhaps it's described formal. Which points at the start of what is assumed as the baseline.

      public void resizeAllToBaseline(double newbaseline)
      Resizes this placeholder and also it's content so that the content described formal fits a new baseline.
